sentences.text: Appearance:
Shri Abhishek Gilke - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Manoj Jain - Advocate for respondent No.1.
 Order

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 07/02/2020 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shajapur (M.P.) in MACC No.400182/2016, whereby an amount of Rs.6,55,000/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition to the appellants / claimants / survivors of the deceased Siddhu Singh with interest @ 6% per annum, who passed away in a road traffic accident,
which took place on 14/05/2016.
2. Learned counsel for the appellants / survivors of the deceased submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- per month only.
At the time of accident deceased was working labourer and was earning Rs.9,000/- per month from the labour work.

His contention is that in case the income of the deceased is not proved by any cogent evidence, income ought to have been assessed on the basis of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8443 2 MA-447-2021 circular issued by Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act, according to which income of the deceased on the date of accident comes to Rs.6,850/- per month considering him as 'Unskilled Labourer'.
2.1

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He further submits that the learned Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding any amount in the head of Loss of Consortium.

His contention is that all the survivors should have been awarded Rs.40,000/- each in the head of Loss of Consortium in the light of para 59.8 of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

3.1 His further contention is that learned Claims Tribunal has erred in deducting 1/4th towards personal expenses, whereas as per para 30 of the judgment in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and followed in para 59.5 of the judgment delivered in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 , instead of 1/4 th, 1/3rd is to be deducted towards personal expenses.

entities.text: Smt. Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from this, all the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.

Hence,
prays NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8443 3 MA-447-2021 for dismissal of the appeal as aforesaid.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that at the time of accident i.e. on 14/05/2016 deceased was working as labourer, however, his income has not been established by adducing cogent evidence, therefore, in the light of the judgment delivered by the apex Court in the case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093, income of the deceased is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, therefore, on the basis of circular income of the deceased is taken as Rs.6,850/- per month for unskilled labour.

entities.text: Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram & Anr. Vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav reported in (2022) 1 SCC 198 : 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3093
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. In the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , Hon'ble the Apex Court in para 59.8 has held that all the survivors of the deceased are entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/- each in the head of loss of consortium, therefore, since the claimants are wife and sons of the deceased, each of them are entitled for an awarded Rs.40,000/- each in this head.

7. As per the judgments in the case of Smt. Sarla Verma (Supra) and para 59.5 of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , where dependents are two to three in number, 1/3 rd amount is to be deducted towards personal expenses.
Learned Claims Tribunal has erred in deducting 1/4 th towards personal expenses, therefore, the same is replaced by deducting 1/3r d towards personal expenses.
Adequate amount has been awarded in other heads, which requires no interference by this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8443 4 MA-447-2021 8.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.6,850/- pm + 25% FP Loss of Dependency: X 12 months - 1/3rd Personal Expenses X Multiplier of 13 = Rs.8,90,500/-
 Loss of Consortium: Rs.1,20,000/-

2  Loss of Estate: Rs.15,000/-
 Funeral Expenses: Rs.15,000/-
 Total: Rs.10,40,500/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.6,55,000/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.3,85,500/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.10,45,500/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.6,55,000/-.

sentences.text:
Accordingly,
the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.3,85,500/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
9. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellants / claimants is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
